title: Presidential Adviser Floats April 16, 2028 as Early Election Date to Enable Third Erdoğan Term
detail: Senior presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum said parliament could call early elections for April 16, 2028 — 'the anniversary of the referendum marking our transition to the presidential system' — which he said would let President Erdoğan run 'for the last time.' Under Article 116, a two-term president becomes eligible for a third term only if parliament, not the president, calls early elections; that requires 360 of 600 votes, and the AKP-MHP bloc (roughly 326 seats) would need about 34 more votes than it currently holds. The proposal follows Erdoğan's September 11 reference to 'approaching elections' and AKP deputy chair Abdulhamit Gül's September 15 remarks; an AKP spokesperson has previously denied early elections are under consideration.
confidenceReason: Reflects one adviser's proposal, not a confirmed parliamentary schedule; AKP has previously denied early elections are planned.

title: Regulator Orders Liquidation of 130 Investment Funds as Selloff Hits BIST-100
detail: Turkey's Capital Markets Board (SPK) ordered the liquidation of 130 investment funds managed by seven portfolio firms (Tera, Pusula, Hedef, Atlas, A1, Pardus and Bulls) and imposed a travel ban on Tera Yatırım Holding chairman Emre Tezmen, after Tera Portföy and Pusula Portföy failed to meet redemption requests on some funds. The crisis stemmed from fund managers concentrating holdings in thinly-traded, affiliated companies — two Pusula funds returned 164% and 144% in the first seven months of 2026 — until new SPK rules in late August forced position reductions and triggered a rush of selling; investors pulled roughly $1 billion from funds on September 16 alone. The BIST-100 fell almost 6% before trading was automatically paused, then recovered about 2.2% after the SPK's intervention was announced; Turkey's central bank provided $6.2 billion in emergency liquidity. Separately, a former Istanbul stock exchange chief was placed under investigation over a public warning issued as stocks fell 6.6%.

title: Turkey Submits Draft Black Sea Civilian Shipping Security Deal to Russia and Ukraine
detail: Turkey submitted a draft memorandum to both Russia and Ukraine proposing an end to attacks on civilian vessels in the Black Sea, modeled on the mechanism of the 2022 Turkey/UN-brokered Black Sea Grain Initiative (which Russia exited in 2023). The proposal focuses on protecting ships along the riskiest 4–5 mile stretch where vessels leave Ukrainian territorial waters and enter international waters, following a sharp rise in drone attacks on commercial shipping — at least 25 Turkish-owned vessels, four Turkish-flagged, have been hit since late June 2026.
confidenceReason: Based on a diplomatic source describing a draft proposal; neither Russia nor Ukraine had publicly responded at time of reporting.
